title: Edge-case layout smoothing for mixed-card grids and ephemeral drawers
creator: Lena Park
description: We need a resilient, graceful reflow strategy for pages that mix dense card grids (cost insights, model rollouts) with ephemeral drawers/modals. Current issues: flicker when drawers open on small widths, charts shifting under fixed headers, and inconsistent column collapse between Chromium and WebKit. Goal is to produce a design spec and interactive prototype that handles edge cases (very narrow widths, scrollable modals, nested drawers) without breaking accessibility or increasing cognitive load.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates stable reflow across 320–1440px with no content overlap or horizontal scroll
Charts maintain baseline visibility and axis labels aren’t truncated at tested breakpoints
Open drawers/panels don’t cause layout jumps; background grids maintain focus states
Behavior is consistent between Chrome, Safari, Firefox on macOS and iOS/Android browsers
Design tokens and spacing scale rules defined so engineering can implement without heavy per-route overrides
design_notes: Prefer progressive collapse (priority-first) for multi-column grids rather than abrupt stack-only behavior
Introduce an ephemeral-nesting guideline: when a drawer is opened above a scrollable grid, lock grid scroll and animate drawer from top with opacity mask to reduce perceived shift
Use CSS containment where possible and request 'will-change: transform' sparingly to avoid GPU thrash on lower-end devices
Chart canvas resizing should use a debounce + placeholder skeleton to avoid reflow flashes; consider offscreen rendering to compute final layout before commit
Provide a tokenized set of breakpoint buckets (compact / medium / roomy) that map to component-level rules rather than ad-hoc media queries
